question:
HLA-DR-restricted T-cell reactivity to amyloid β (Aβ) has been associated with Alzheimers disease (AD), but structural evidence for HLA presentation of Aβ-derived peptides remains elusive.

Three candidate results follow. Exactly one is what this study reported.
- Result A: We present the crystal structure of the Aβ1-15 fragment bound to HLA-DR1, providing, to the best of our knowledge, the first experimental structure of an Alzheimers Aβ peptide bound to an HLA molecule. The molecular architecture of this complex defines a peptide:MHC interaction dictated by engagement of Aβ1-15 peptide central core with further involvement of N- and C-terminal peptide flanks. The structure reveals that DRβ1 Arg70, a polymorphic position, directly binds P4 and P5 through polar contacts, providing a rationale for HLA-DRB allelic bias underpinning accommodation of Aβ1-15. We also describe the Aβ1-15:HLA-DRB1 surface topology, informing a candidate binding surface for potential T-cell recognition. Collectively, these findings contribute a structural framework for further research in the context of Aβ-specific CD4+ T-cell autoreactivity in AD.
- Result B: We present the crystal structure of the Aβ1-15 fragment bound to HLA-DR1, providing, to the best of our knowledge, the first experimental structure of an Alzheimers Aβ peptide bound to an HLA molecule. The molecular architecture of this complex defines a peptide:MHC interaction dictated by engagement of Aβ1-15 peptide central core with further involvement of N- and C-terminal peptide flanks. The structure reveals that DRβ1 Arg70, a polymorphic position, directly binds P4 and P5 through van der Waals contacts, providing a rationale for HLA-DRB allelic bias underpinning accommodation of Aβ1-15. We also describe the Aβ1-15:HLA-DRB1 surface topology, informing a candidate binding surface for potential T-cell recognition. Collectively, these findings contribute a structural framework for further research in the context of Aβ-specific CD4+ T-cell autoreactivity in AD.
- Result C: We present the crystal structure of the Aβ1-15 fragment bound to HLA-DR1, providing, to the best of our knowledge, the first experimental structure of an Alzheimers Aβ peptide bound to an HLA molecule. The molecular architecture of this complex defines a peptide:MHC interaction dictated by engagement of the N- and C-terminal peptide flanks with further involvement of the Aβ1-15 central core. The structure reveals that DRβ1 Arg70, a polymorphic position, does not directly engage P4 or P5, with polar contacts to these positions instead mediated by conserved framework residues, indicating that accommodation of Aβ1-15 is independent of HLA-DRB allelic bias at this position. We also describe the Aβ1-15:HLA-DRB1 surface topology, informing a candidate binding surface for potential T-cell recognition. Collectively, these findings contribute a structural framework for further research in the context of Aβ-specific CD4+ T-cell autoreactivity in AD.
Which result did this study report? Rank the candidates, and give the mechanism, the key evidence, and a validation experiment for the top pick.
